$comment: Shared state for ONE work-graph run. Lives at .graph/runs/<run-id>/state.json. Every node reads this on start and appends to its OWN key on finish - the builder writes its own builders.<slice> key, including the branch it worked on. Never rewrite another node's key. Every node key carries written_by, naming the node that wrote it: that is the ONLY record of authorship this file has, and without it 'never rewrite another node's key' is unverifiable - an orchestrator hand-writing all six keys is indistinguishable from six nodes doing their jobs. verify-state.py --audit checks it. This file is the edge: it is how context crosses between agents that cannot see each other.

unknowns: Does lazy-per-run loading violate the refetch constraint? CLAUDE.md line 135-137 states 'Node/node click selection never triggers a refetch', and testRouterDeepLinkAndClicks at test.js:404 asserts zero fetches on selection. But /api/run?id=X returning only one run would require a fetch when user clicks a run not in the light list, violating this rule. Three possible resolutions: (a) prefetch the selected run as part of initial load (defeating lazy optimization), (b) keep only the most-recently-selected run's full state in memory and reuse it for same-run selections, or (c) interpret the rule narrowly as 'no refetch while using an already-loaded run' rather than 'no refetch to load a new run'.

How does the light-run payload impact the silent refresh logic? Line 1376 compares the full response for equality; splitting /api/graph would require updating this fingerprinting or implementing per-run etags.
Must _path be in the light list? It renders in the detail header at line 980; omitting it would require fetching the run's full state to display the path, or changing the UI.
Should written_by be rendered? Every state.json key carries it per schema; the page currently shows zero node attribution. The architect will decide if this is meaningful UX or noise.

Is there a race condition in activity.jsonl reading? The fleet appends while the request reads; a partial line is tolerated (line 274) but the final 40-event slice computed at line 303 could include an event written after read-start. Acceptable as-designed but worth noting.
risks: PLAN-KILLER: testRouterDeepLinkAndClicks line 404 enforces 'run/node selection must never trigger a refetch'. A split design with /api/run?id=X violates this when clicking a run not in the light list. The architect must either (1) abandon lazy-loading and return all runs, (2) prefetch the clicked run's full state on initial load (defeating optimization), (3) permit refetches for *new* run selection (requiring test change) but not for node selection within a run, or (4) cache the selected run client-side after fetch and silently fail on out-of-cache selection.

testSilentPollSkipsRenderWhenNothingChanged at line 542 relies on whole-response comparison at line 1376. If /api/graph is split, the fingerprinting logic must adapt or the optimization (skip render when fleet hasn't moved) breaks.

buildAnonMap() at line 348 needs all run.app values; if the light list exists, it must include app in every run or anonymization will miss identities. This is likely acceptable but constrains the light-list schema.

activity.jsonl is read in full on every 4s poll (serve.py:249); the tail is cheap but the read cost remains. A size-based cache for unchanged runs would require server-side state, conflicting with the stateless design.

plan.intent: Make /api/graph a conditional request. serve.py computes a strong ETag as a hash of the serialized payload with the `generated` field excluded, returns it on every 200, and answers 304 with an empty body when If-None-Match matches. index.html stores the last ETag, sends If-None-Match on every fetch, and treats 304 as the existing nothing-changed branch (renderStamp, then return). Chooses transfer + client-CPU savings on the poll over splitting the payload; see rationale.

plan.intent: Render the three shipped-but-unused fields as decided signals, not dumped strings. (a) _mtime: relative age of the run's state.json in the run detail header, worded as "state written 4m ago" and never as "idle" -- nodes only write state.json on finish while activity.jsonl moves continuously -- and flagged only when status is in ACTIVE_STATUSES (index.html:279) AND both _mtime and the last _activity event are stale. That turns it into the wedged-run signal, which status alone cannot give. (b) scope_exceptions: a warning-styled block in the run detail, shown only when at least one entry is a real path; entries that are the schema docstring (ORCHESTRATOR-OWNED...) or an orchestrator WHY rationale are not exceptions and must not be counted. (c) written_by: a per-node provenance mark on the graph with four states -- stamped correctly (quiet); missing (legacy run predating the field: muted, never an alarm); still carrying the template placeholder "the node that wrote this key..." (that node did not run: muted); and a value naming a DIFFERENT node (loud -- this is the forgery signal verify-state.py --audit looks for).

Same trap on scope_exceptions, where the docstring entry makes a zero-exception run look like a one-exception run. Shares index.html and test.js with s1.

architect.edges: s1 -> s2, but this is FILE CONTENTION, not an artifact dependency. s2 consumes nothing s1 produces; they are serialized only because both edit index.html and test.js. The order is reversible. Recorded as a serialization constraint rather than a data edge, per the no-fake-edges rule.
architect.rationale: DECISION: conditional requests (ETag/304). Do NOT split the payload. Measured on the real fleet (9 runs): total payload 691,262 B, of which runs are 684,346 B (99%) and all fleet-wide keys together are 6,934 B (1%). Largest single run 192,192 B = 27.8% of the whole. (1) REFETCH INVARIANT: 304 preserves it completely -- same URL, same body whenever the body changes, zero router changes, testRouterDeepLinkAndClicks (test.js:404) untouched. A split breaks it: clicking a run whose heavy keys were not shipped must either fetch (violating CLAUDE.md:135-137 and that test) or render a detail pane that never fills. All four of the scout's resolutions either destroy the saving (prefetch), help only re-selection (client cache), or require relaxing a constraint stated as not-mine-to-relax. (2) WHAT IT SAVES: an unchanged poll goes 691,262 B -> ~200 B of headers, i.e. 100% of the repeated transfer. It also removes two client costs not named in the brief: the JSON.parse at index.html:1373 AND the JSON.stringify of the whole payload inside payloadFingerprint (index.html:1314-1316), which today runs on every poll INCLUDING the ones that change nothing -- so an unchanged poll currently costs parse + stringify of ~1.4 MB on the browser main thread every 4 seconds. That CPU, not the localhost bytes, is the real win. The split's saving is bounded by the selected run: 691 KB -> 196 KB (72%) with the biggest run selected, and -> 18 KB (97%) with a small one. As anticipated, when a large run is selected that run IS most of the payload, so the split has a floor it cannot cross; 304 reaches zero. (3) COMPLEXITY: 304 is one hash server-side plus one header and a status branch client-side, and it lands on the unchanged path that already exists at index.html:1388. No new endpoint, no run cache, no invalidation. The split needs a new endpoint, a client run cache, per-run staleness handling, rework of the fingerprint (scout risk 2), and an app-in-every-light-row constraint for buildAnonMap (scout risk 3, fact 22) -- several load-bearing behaviours moving at once. (4) LIVE RUN -- the sharpest axis, and it partly cuts against 304, stated plainly: while a run is actively being written the token changes and 304 correctly misses, so it gives nothing exactly when the poll is busiest. But the hit rate is already empirically known -- the author's own comment at index.html:1311-1313 says the unchanged case is the common case while a node is thinking -- and deriving the ETag from the same bytes the fingerprint covers makes the 304 hit rate IDENTICAL to the fingerprint hit rate already observed. The split, by contrast, has no unchanged-detection at all: it re-ships the selected run every 4s whether it moved or not, and fixing that means adding per-run ETags, i.e. building this mechanism anyway on top of the split. That is decisive: the split needs 304 to be good; 304 does not need the split. (5) GROWTH -- the one axis the split wins, decisively, and 304 loses. 304 does not stop growth: first load, fleet switch, Refresh and every changed poll still ship all history; at 50 runs that is ~3.8 MB. A light list would be ~451 B/run, ~22.5 KB at 50. Accepted deliberately: 691 KB on localhost on first load is not a problem today, and buying the growth fix costs a stated invariant. Named revisit trigger: when runs exceed ~40 or the payload exceeds ~2 MB, reopen this WITH an explicit decision to amend CLAUDE.md:135-137 first -- and note that archiving old runs out of .graph/runs/ solves it at zero cost to FleetView. ETAG CONSTRUCTION -- rejecting the token proposed in the brief: max state.json mtime + run count + registry mtime is the wrong token. It misses agents/*.md, skills/*/SKILL.md, siblings and the multi-fleet dimension, and mtime granularity admits FALSE 304s on sub-second writes during an active run. A false 304 is a permanently stale live view -- strictly worse than a large payload, and the opposite of what this app is for. A hash of the serialized payload minus the generated field cannot produce a false 304 by construction: same hash iff same bytes. The cost is that server CPU is unchanged, since you must assemble in order to hash. Accepted: this is a localhost viewer with one reader, so the scarce resource is the browser main thread, not the Python process. STATELESSNESS, against the sentence flagged: this adds NO server-side state. The token is derived from the body of the request being served and recomputed from disk every time; the client holds the only copy. The sentence no cache to invalidate and no state held between requests (CLAUDE.md:32-33) survives literally. OPTIONAL IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: old client + new server sends no If-None-Match and always gets 200; new client + old server sees no ETag, stores nothing, always gets 200. The builder must also settle how the Cache-Control: no-store header (serve.py:389) and the fetch cache:no-store option (index.html:1372) interact with conditional requests -- the end-to-end done_when is what proves it. SHAPE: single-loop, and not close. Both slices edit index.html and test.js, and s1 inherently spans serve.py AND index.html because an ETag with no client sending If-None-Match saves nothing. There is no disjoint file partition, so there is no diamond -- it is a sequence, and fanning out would guarantee the fan-in conflict. Both slices are risk:high for the reasons recorded on each; neither is merely small. MOBILE: the registry lists fleetview as ui desktop-only, so conventions/mobile-first.md does not apply and is deliberately skipped. CORRECTION TO A FACT IN THE BRIEF (flagged, does not change the plan): the run with 7 scope_exceptions is 2026-09-02-date-accuracy (7 real paths). 2026-09-01-huntstack-mobile has 2 entries, only 1 of which is a path -- the other is an orchestrator WHY rationale. And this run's own state.json has 1 entry that is the schema docstring, i.e. zero real exceptions. This strengthens rather than changes s2: it is precisely why the count must filter rather than call len().
not_doing: NOT splitting /api/graph into a light run list plus /api/run?id=X. It is the only option that stops payload growth, and it is refused because it cannot be built without breaking the rule that node/run click selection never triggers a refetch (CLAUDE.md:135-137) and the test that enforces it (test.js:404). Doing less on purpose: the growth ceiling is accepted and given an explicit revisit trigger (>~40 runs or >~2 MB) rather than chased now.

NOT fixing collect_activity's full read (serve.py:249). Measured: ~151 KB of activity.jsonl across 5 files read and parsed per request to yield ~16 KB of summary and tail. Note this is an I/O cost, NOT a payload cost -- _activity is only ~4 KB per run, so it is not why the payload is 691 KB. Any real fix (a size or mtime keyed incremental read) needs server-side memory between requests, contradicting no cache to invalidate and no state held between requests. A local 151 KB read every 4s is not worth that design sentence. Also: 304 does NOT remove this cost, since the payload must be assembled to be hashed -- stated so nobody assumes s1 covered it.

NOT rewriting collect_activity's tail accumulation to a bounded deque. It would cut peak memory from O(all events) to O(40) in one safe pass, but it fixes memory, which nobody reported, not the read cost that was raised. Scope creep; recorded here so it is a choice rather than an oversight.
NOT removing _mtime from the payload. It is 34 B per run and s2 gives it a job.

NOT adding a mtime-derived fast-path token to skip payload assembly on a 304, even though it would also remove the collect_activity read. Rejected because it reintroduces the false-304 risk that the content hash exists to eliminate.

NOT touching the router, the fleet switcher, selectedRun/selectedNode, or Anonymize. buildAnonMap keeps every run's app field because every run still ships in full, so scout fact 22 / risk 3 is moot under this design.
NOT adding pagination, archiving or run retention to FleetView. It is a read-only viewer; run retention is the fleet's business, not the viewer's.

scope_exceptions: WHY (orchestrator, 2026-09-04): the human approved changing the /api/graph transport contract, and fleetview/CLAUDE.md is the file that documents that contract (the Architecture section describes the single fetch and the 4s poll) as well as the accepted payload-growth ceiling and its revisit trigger. Documenting an approved change is intrinsic to it, but the architect's plan[].files omitted the path, so the scope guard would deny it. This grants NOTHING beyond recording work already approved at the gate. Any slice that writes it MUST set deviation_from_approved_plan.

On a scratch two-fleet setup, 6 sub-second edits gave 6 distinct ETags; a touch, a new run dir and an activity.jsonl append each moved it. A false 304 is unreachable: the hash covers a superset of payloadFingerprint. Fleet A's ETag against fleet B -> 200, B's -> 304. W/, comma lists and * parse; garbage falls through to 200. findings.issue: Doc precision, not behaviour: the Architecture paragraph says the ETag is 'a SHA-256 of exactly the bytes that response ships, minus generated'. serve.py:449-452 pops `generated`, hashes json.dumps of the rest, then re-adds `generated` at the END of the dict, so the 200 body's key order is fleet,fleets,active_fleet_id,portfolio,siblings,agents,skills,runs,generated -- verified on a live response. The hashed serialization is therefore not a substring of the shipped bytes. Correctness is unaffected (the client reads by key, and I confirmed the ETag is stable across two 200s whose bodies differ only in `generated`), but the sentence overstates the relationship. Suggest 'a SHA-256 of the response's content with `generated` removed'.

Behaviour change outside the silent-poll path, believed intended but unrecorded: the fingerprint short-circuit at line 1412 is gated on opts.silent, but the new 304 branch is not. So the Refresh button (line 1451, non-silent) now returns without calling renderAll() when the server answers 304, where before this slice it always rebuilt the DOM. No wrong render results -- DATA is by definition current and the stamp still moves -- but Refresh loses its incidental force-a-redraw affordance. The architect's rationale does say 304 'lands on the unchanged path that already exists', so this reads as intended; worth one sentence in CLAUDE.md if it is.

Unreachable except branch: the second `try: body = json.dumps(payload)` / `except (TypeError, ValueError)` at serve.py:465-469 cannot fire. The same dict minus one string key already serialized successfully at line 451, and re-adding the popped `generated` string cannot introduce a non-serializable value. Harmless and symmetric with the first block, so not worth churn on its own; noted so a future reader does not assume it is load-bearing. Related and also benign: `payload.pop('generated', '')` means a build_payload that ever stopped emitting `generated` would silently ship an empty string rather than omit the key; renderStamp guards on falsiness, so it renders ''.

Coverage observation, not a defect: payload_etag() and etag_matches() have no automated test. test.js drives index.html in a vm and models the server with a fetch shim, so the entire server half of the transport contract rests on the manual e2e gate. That matches the app -- there is no Python test rig at all, by design per CLAUDE.md 'Stdlib and vanilla only' -- and I compensated by exercising the parser by hand against a live server: matching, weak (W/), comma-list and * forms all returned 304 0, while an unparseable value and another fleet's ETag both fell through to a full 200. findings.issue: Surviving mutant: deleting the ACTIVE_STATUSES guard from wedgedFor (index.html:476) leaves the suite GREEN at 118/0. The assertion that names the rule -- `a done run is never flagged as wedged` -- sits on a fixture whose _mtime is 4m old and which has no _activity at all, so it cannot fail for that reason. The implementation is correct; the coverage is not. Concrete consequence if the guard is ever dropped: all 7 `done` runs in this fleet render a red `no state or activity for 10d` pill and the gate still passes. Add one fixture: status=done, _mtime 40m old, _activity.tail[0].t 40m old -> assert no flag.

ACTIVE_STATUSES includes `awaiting-approval`, so a run parked at the human gate for over 15 minutes -- which also stops its activity.jsonl, because it is waiting on a person -- renders the red `no state or activity for 3h` pill. That run is not wedged, it is blocked on a human. This matches the architect's intent verbatim (it names ACTIVE_STATUSES), so it is not a deviation, but it is the one predictable false positive left in the signal. No run in the fleet is currently at that status, so nothing lights up today.

realScopeExceptions() calls .filter on run.scope_exceptions without a shape check. A state.json where the key is a string or an object throws `.filter is not a function` inside renderRunDetail, which truncates the run detail to the header panel and raises a false `Could not reach /api/graph` banner. I verified the surrounding code fails identically today for a non-array architect.plan (`plan.map is not a function`) and log (`logItems.map`), and _schema.json types the field as an array, so this matches the house pattern rather than introducing a new one. Note, not a blocker. The poll still reschedules through it (timers=[4000] confirmed).

isRealPath rejects any entry containing whitespace, so a genuinely granted path with a space (`huntstack/apps/My App/src/x.ts`) or a bare directory with neither separator nor extension (`node_modules`) renders as zero exceptions and the warning block disappears entirely. That is the silent direction of the filter -- an under-warn, not an over-warn. No path in this umbrella has a space today, and the trade-off is stated in the comment, so this is a note. Worth one assertion if a space-bearing path is ever granted.

The CLAUDE.md correction is accurate -- I read serve.py:450-464 and confirmed `generated` is popped, the remainder serialized and hashed, then re-added, so the hashed string is genuinely not a substring of the shipped body. But payload_etag's own docstring still carries the exact wording CLAUDE.md just retired: `Hashed over exactly the bytes the 200 would ship minus generated`. serve.py is outside s2's file set and outside the scope_exception, so leaving it is correct here; flag it for a later slice so the two do not disagree.

relSpan cosmetics, verified across -100000..864000s: no NaN, no negative span, monotone. A future _mtime (clock skew) clamps to `state written 0s ago` rather than disclosing the skew -- graceful, and the title attribute still carries the raw _mtime, but the page silently asserts something false. Deleting the Math.max(0,...) clamp is the second surviving mutant: the suite stays GREEN, so nothing tests the skew case. Also 44.6s renders `45s` and 45s renders `1m`. The builder's note that ages are measured against the browser clock is disclosed in builders.s2 but not on the page; acceptable for a localhost viewer.

findings.issue: Fix 3 covers the wrong TYPE but not wrong MEMBERS. scope_exceptions:[{"path":"huntstack/apps/mobile"}] or [42,null] is an Array, so scopeExceptionsMalformed() is false and realScopeExceptions() filters every member out -> the run renders NO scope-exceptions block at all, byte-identical to a run that granted nothing. Verified by rendering: junk-members-only gives block:no, banner:no, paths:[]. A mixed array ([42,"fleetview/CLAUDE.md"]) does render the real path and silently drops the junk, so the count can read "1 path" for a 2-entry array. Not a blocker: _schema.json types entries as strings, no run on this fleet has a non-string member, it does not crash, and the direction the finding was raised about (the whole value being the wrong type) is fixed and tested. Cheapest fix: count non-string members and add them to the malformed banner.

Fix 4 loosened isRealPath in the over-report direction and CLAUDE.md does not say so. The new gate is: not opening with WHY/ORCHESTRATOR-OWNED, <=160 chars, no terminal .,;:!?, no sentence break, <=4 whitespace tokens, contains a separator or an extension. So a rationale fragment that does not begin with the word WHY is counted as a granted path: "Approved: huntstack/apps/mobile/**", "granted for s1/s2 only", "orchestrator grant: fleetview/CLAUDE.md" and "the human approved graph_agents/CLAUDE.md" all return true (I ran them). With scope_exceptions:["fleetview/CLAUDE.md","Approved: huntstack/apps/mobile/**"] the block reads "2 paths a builder was allowed to write" and lists the rationale as one of them - it misreports what the human gate let through. It holds on real data only because the WHY( prefix is kept by convention; _schema.json says "say why", it does not mandate the token. CLAUDE.md states the mechanism ("a sentence is long, punctuated and made of clauses") but not this failure mode. Note, not a blocker - no such entry exists on this fleet and all five ground-truth counts are exact - but the honest-documentation requirement is not met until one line names it.

Under-report margins of the same heuristic, also undocumented. A bare directory with neither separator nor extension is dropped: node_modules -> false, dist -> false, so a grant recorded as a directory name renders zero exceptions and the block disappears. A genuinely spaced path with 5+ tokens is dropped (huntstack/apps/A B C D E/x.ts -> false; the 4-token huntstack/apps/My New Mobile App/src/x.ts survives). A path longer than 160 chars is dropped. A path whose first segment is literally why/ is eaten by PROSE_OPENER ("why: fleetview/serve.py" -> false, /^WHY /i matches). Glob src/** and Windows fleetview\serve.py both correctly return true. All contrived; recording the boundary so the next reader does not re-derive it.
